nodes.content: Design a distributed scheduler preserving tenant quota ownership and performance isolation during tenant migration, adversarial workloads, and network partitions.
requirements: Quota ownership never duplicates during migration, crashes, or partitions; disconnected schedulers cannot exceed assigned quotas.
On healthy workers, unaffected tenants’ p99 dispatch latency remains within 2× their workload-matched isolated baseline.

nodes.content: Use Raft-backed quota escrows, reclaim only after worker-wide epoch fencing, and isolate dispatch with per-tenant queues and CPU budgets.
How can escrow transfer fence a partitioned scheduler before workers accept dispatches under reassigned quotas?
Reassigning escrow only after every worker durably acknowledges a tenant-epoch fence prevents overlapping quota use during partitions.
Freeze tenant dispatch, drain in-flight quota, collect durable fence acknowledgments from every eligible worker, then commit escrow transfer.
Run 10,000 PartitionFence fault schedules with migrations, crashes, and partitions; check escrow overlap and quota-limit violations.
PartitionFence’s 10,000 fault schedules found zero overlapping escrow owners and zero quota-limit violations with durable epoch fencing.
Require durable worker epoch acknowledgments before escrow reassignment, based on PartitionFence’s zero ownership overlaps and quota-limit violations.
Implement approved durable fence collection in migration; run PartitionMove to compare unaffected-tenant p99 against isolated baseline and detect escrow overlap.
PartitionMove found unaffected-tenant p99 dispatch at 18 ms versus 6 ms isolated on healthy workers, despite zero escrow overlaps.
Worker-enforced 30-second escrow leases with a 100 ms clock-skew margin prevent overlapping quota use without partitioned-worker acknowledgments.
Model-check LeaseSkew with migrations, crashes, partitions, 100 ms clock skew, and 30-second worker leases; count overlapping quota use.
LeaseSkew checked 50,000 partition-and-migration schedules under 100 ms clock skew; worker-enforced leases produced zero overlapping quota use.
Combine durable escrow fencing with worker-local dispatch reservations and migration rate limits, targeting unaffected-tenant p99 ≤12 ms.
Does migration traffic monopolize worker admission slots, raising unaffected-tenant p99 to 18 ms despite per-tenant queues?
Measure admission-slot occupancy in PartitionMove; cap migration traffic at 20% and compare unaffected-tenant p99 to the 6 ms baseline.
Using PartitionFence-validated fencing, run PartitionMove with 20% migration admission cap and worker-local reservations; measure slot occupancy, p99, escrow overlap.
PartitionMove: migration occupied 18% of admission slots; unaffected-tenant p99 was 10 ms versus 6 ms isolated; zero escrow overlaps.
PartitionMove report contains slot-occupancy traces, unaffected-tenant p99 comparisons, and escrow-overlap checks for capped migration dispatch.
Audit the PartitionMove report against raw healthy-worker admission logs, verifying migration-cap accounting, unaffected-tenant p99, and workload-matched baselines.
Raw-log audit confirmed 10 ms unaffected-tenant p99 versus workload-matched 6 ms isolated, with migration slot occupancy 18% on healthy workers.
Adopt fenced escrows, worker-local reservations, and a 20% migration cap: audited p99 was 10 versus 6 ms isolated.
Replace PartitionMove diagnosis with 24-hour adversarial partition soaks of the adopted 20% cap, checking zero overlaps and p99 ≤2× baseline.
Run 24-hour AdversarialSoak with burst floods, migration churn, crashes, and partitions; measure escrow overlaps and healthy-worker unaffected-tenant p99.
AdversarialSoak report supersedes PartitionMove report with 24-hour burst-and-partition traces, escrow-overlap counts, and healthy-worker p99-to-isolated ratios.
Use worker-enforced 30-second quota leases, clock-skew-safe handoffs, and per-tenant fair admission to preserve partition safety and isolation.
Under ≤100 ms clock skew, 30-second worker leases prevent quota overlaps, while fair admission keeps unaffected p99 ≤2× isolated.
Do synchronized lease renewals during partition recovery saturate admission slots and push unaffected-tenant p99 above 2× isolated?
Run RecoveryBurst post-partition with synchronized 30-second lease renewals, 100 ms skew, and fair admission; measure quota overlaps and unaffected-tenant p99/isolation.
RecoveryBurst found zero quota overlaps, but synchronized renewals raised unaffected-tenant p99 to 15 ms versus 6 ms isolated.
Trace renewal admission-slot occupancy in RecoveryBurst, then stagger renewals by 0–5 seconds; compare unaffected-tenant p99 and quota overlaps.
RecoveryBurst with 0–5-second staggered renewals achieved unaffected-tenant p99 of 10 ms versus 6 ms isolated, with zero quota overlaps.
Combine fenced escrows, 20% migration admission caps, and 0–5-second staggered renewals with worker-local reservations.
Do simultaneous capped migrations and staggered renewals exceed the 12 ms unaffected-tenant p99 limit during partition recovery?
With migration capped at 20% and renewals staggered 0–5 seconds, combined recovery keeps unaffected-tenant p99 ≤12 ms.
Using RecoveryBurst’s 15 ms synchronized and 10 ms staggered results, test concurrent 20%-capped migrations for p99 and escrow overlaps.
Run CombinedRecovery with 20%-capped migrations and 0–5-second staggered renewals; compare healthy-worker unaffected-tenant p99 against 6 ms isolated; count escrow overlaps.
CombinedRecovery measured unaffected-tenant p99 at 11 ms versus 6 ms isolated during concurrent migration and recovery; escrow overlaps remained zero.
CombinedRecovery report records migration-cap traces, staggered renewal timings, healthy-worker p99-to-isolated ratios, and escrow-overlap checks.
Audit CombinedRecovery report against raw worker admission and escrow logs; verify 20% cap, renewal staggering, p99 baseline, and ownership.
Raw-log audit confirmed CombinedRecovery’s 11 ms unaffected-tenant p99 versus 6 ms isolated, 20% migration cap, staggered renewals, zero overlaps.
Adopt capped migration plus staggered renewals with fenced escrows: audited combined recovery met 11 ms p99 and zero overlaps.
Use Raft-issued, worker-enforced quota subleases with expiry-guarded migration and reserved renewal lanes to isolate tenant dispatch.
Can a 5% reserved renewal lane absorb synchronized sublease refreshes while keeping unaffected-tenant p99 at or below 12 ms?
Replay synchronized 30-second sublease renewals with a 5% reserved lane; compare healthy-worker unaffected p99 against 6 ms isolated.
Replay synchronized sublease renewals using AdversarialSoak and CombinedRecovery traces; measure 5% lane occupancy and unaffected-tenant p99.
RenewalLane replay report contains 5% lane-occupancy traces and healthy-worker unaffected-tenant p99 against the 6 ms isolated baseline.
Audit RenewalLane replay against source traces and lease-expiry logs; assess 5% lane saturation, p99 ≤12 ms, and quota overlap.
RenewalLane audit found 4.6% peak lane occupancy, 11 ms unaffected-tenant p99 versus 6 ms isolated, and zero quota overlaps.
Adopt the 5% reserved renewal lane: audited peak occupancy was 4.6%, unaffected p99 was 11 ms, and overlaps were zero.
